turnaround_reason: Ag-chemical destocking plus a looming Rynaxypyr patent cliff took FMC down ~90% from its 2022 highs. Thesis is that channel inventories are normalizing (on-farm use now exceeding distributor sales) and a new-AI product ramp offsets branded erosion.
bullish_points: Destocking cycle appears to be ending — actual on-farm use now exceeds distributor sales, signaling channel normalization
New active ingredients (Isoflex, fluindapyr, Dodhylex, rimisoxafen) projected at $300-400M in 2026, ~75%+ growth vs 2025
Q2 2026 beat (EPS 0.26 vs 0.22); cheap on forward earnings (fwd P/E ~6.9, P/B ~0.87), near 52w low $9.95
Analyst target mean $13.4 (~18% upside), technical double-bottom noted near crisis lows
bearish_points: Rynaxypyr patent cliff hitting in 2026 — branded earnings only flat at best as generics erode price; this is a structural, not cyclical, headwind
TTM profit margin deeply negative (-85%) on impairments; revenue still declining -17.5%
Heavy debt (~$4.4B, D/E 265) into a still-uneven recovery; LatAm patented markets lagging as distributors wait for cheaper generics
EV/EBITDA ~19.9 on depressed EBITDA — not obviously cheap on cash earnings, only on forward hope
catalyst: Confirmation that destocking is fully behind and new-AI volume growth is outrunning Rynaxypyr generic erosion
suggested_trade: Small-to-medium starter spot $10.50-11.50 (already a watchlist name); this is a cyclical-bottom bet with a patent-cliff offset — keep dry powder for a re-test of the lows.
key_risk: Rynaxypyr generic erosion outpaces the new-product ramp and the recovery stays uneven, leaving earnings and the debt load stuck.
would_skip_if: Q3 shows new-AI sales missing the $300-400M trajectory or Rynaxypyr pricing collapsing faster than volumes can offset.
